summary: On Monday, the New York Times sued Brave in federal court in Manhattan. The complaint alleges that Brave scraped Times content and distributed it to customers the suit names as Anthropic, Perplexity, Mistral, xAI, and Cohere. The Daily News, the Chicago Tribune, and the Orlando Sentinel filed a similar suit the same day. The Times complaint says Brave built an index of more than 30 billion pages with a crawler publishers could not identify or block. It also targets a paywall-bypass feature, and Brave's practice of blocking publisher ads while selling its own. The Times seeks an injunction and damages. TechCrunch says Brave had not responded.

whyItMatters: This is a complaint, not a ruling. If you use Brave's AI answers, or an assistant that buys pages through that index, the suit is about whether that pipeline can keep using publisher sites. A paywall bypass in the browser is part of what the Times is asking a court to stop. Nothing has been ordered yet.
